news.title: Vals, backed by Andreessen Horowitz, is looking to become the gold standard for AI benchmarking
news.summary: Vals AI is hoping to make AI benchmarking a more neutral and trustworthy resource in a world increasingly inundated by AI models.

spec.title: Vals wants to be the gold standard for AI benchmarking

claims.text: Vals is a startup formed in 2024 that says legacy benchmarking systems are being outwitted by AI companies.
Last month Vals raised $40 million in a Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz.
Vals does not publicly disclose its test materials and evaluates models on tasks in law, finance and coding.
evidence_terms: doesn’t publicly disclose its specific test materials

claims.text: Companies pay Vals to test their models, which its founder compares to students paying the College Board to take the SAT.
evidence_terms: Companies pay Vals to test their models

claims.text: Vals' revenue is eight times what it was last year and its team has tripled to 25 people.
evidence_terms: eight times what it was last year

scenes: Wide studio shot, the presenter faces camera and speaks calmly; a lower-third graphic reads 'Vals AI: the new benchmark for benchmarks'.
Close-up, the presenter gestures toward a side panel graphic showing '$40M Series A, led by Andreessen Horowitz' with a 2024 founding date beneath.
Side view, the presenter turns to a floating graphic listing 'Private test sets' and three domain icons labeled Law, Finance, Coding.
Wide studio shot, the presenter wraps up as an on-screen counter animates '8x revenue' and 'team tripled to 25'.
spec.script: If you have ever wondered whether AI benchmarks can be gamed, you are not alone. Vals, a startup founded in 2024, says legacy benchmarks are being outwitted and wants to fix that. Last month it raised 40 million dollars in a Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz. Its approach: keep the test materials private, and grade models on real tasks in law, finance and coding. Companies pay Vals to be tested, a bit like students paying for the SAT. Revenue is now eight times last year's, and the team has tripled to 25.
